ana_sales: Quick Q — customer (regulatory fintech) wants a POC that guarantees EU + APAC data residency. They also want clarity on which subprocessors touch data, how routing/fallback works (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and any pricing uplift for regional pinning. Can ops/solutions/legal chime in? :wave:

lina_pm: Thanks Ana — do they need strict no-cross-border egress (i.e., all egress/logging stays in-region), or is 'control plane in US, data in-region' acceptable?

ana_sales: They said 'no egress outside customer-owned country/region for production', POC can be relaxed but need clear limits. Also asking about timeline to get BYOK enabled for EU.

kevin_sol: Short answers: region list we support: `eu-west-1 (Ireland)`, `eu-central-1 (Frankfurt)`, `asia-northeast-1 (Tokyo)`, `ap-northeast-1 (Seoul)`, `ap-southeast-1 (Singapore)`, `ca-central-1 (Canada)`. Subprocessors: cloud infra (GCP/Azure/AWS depending on region), CDN & monitoring providers (we provide a trimmed list). For Hosted API default routing is nearest-region with failover to nearest compatible region; Dedicated can be pinned to a region/zone (no cross-region KV/cache egress if pinned). BYOK for EU typically ~5 business days to provision once legal/contract done.

kevin_sol: Example call for region pinning (POC param):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
  -H 'X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1' 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-16k","input":"..."}'
```

malik_sre: Ops notes: Hosted fallback logic: prefer same-country endpoints -> same-region endpoints -> nearest-region. If the customer's policy is strict 'no egress outside region', hosted is tricky (we can restrict routing but some control-plane signals may cross borders). Dedicated/Private gives deterministic data path. For POC we can run a shadow test where traffic is pinned and we capture network traces. Also call out that logging/telemetry retention can be configured to stay in-region. :ok_hand:

malik_sre: Cost note: regional pin + reserved capacity typically adds an uplift vs default hosted. Ballpark: Dedicated reservation + regional pin ~25–40% depending on GPU type and locality (APAC tends to be higher). BYOK + compliance attestations are additional line items.

legal_jane: On subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date subprocessor list (will provide CSV). For EU-only production commitments we need a contract addendum (data residency SLA + subprocessors list + data processing addendum). We cannot guarantee zero US control-plane metadata unless using Private with on-prem control plane.

ops_oncall_bot: Created presales ticket #POC-1327 and scheduled runbook workspace: https://internal.redwood/insights/POC-1327 — assigned to @malik_sre and @kevin_sol. ETA: initial runbook draft by EOD tomorrow.

ana_sales: Helpful — thanks. Two asks: (1) can we get the subprocessor CSV + a short one-page summary for the customer's compliance team? (2) can we give a ballpark written % uplift for the deck?

kevin_sol: I can do the one-pager and cost ballpark. Draft will include: regional list, subproc CSV, failover behavior, BYOK ETA, and uplifts: Hosted w/ geo-preference = baseline; Dedicated + regional pin = ~+30% (range +20–40%); BYOK & extended retention = add'l fixed fees.

malik_sre: I'll attach a short runbook snippet and an ops checklist for the POC (keys, certs, tunnel checks, ip allowlists). We should propose a short shadow test first to prove no-evidence-of-egress outside region.

lina_pm: Plan for handoff: kevin to prepare one-pager + pricing, malik to prepare runbook & traces script, legal to attach subproc CSV and clause draft. We'll sync with customer on Thu 9am CET.

ana_sales: Perfect — putting call on calendar. TY all. :thumbsup:
